_README: Values that are correct in a non-English lang/ file BECAUSE they are identical to English. Read by scripts/check-php-lang-untranslated.mjs. Keyed by VALUE, never by key path: the same invariant string appears under many keys, and a per-key list would become a suppression list nobody reads. `global` applies to every locale; `byLocale` is for cognates and borrowings that are right in one language and wrong in the others. Seeded from IDENTICAL_VALUE_ALLOWLIST / LANGUAGE_IDENTICAL_VALUE_ALLOWLIST in scripts/translate-i18n-gaps.mjs, which had already been curated for the React JSON locales. Adding an entry is a claim that a translator would leave it alone — not a way to make the gate quiet.
_CURATION_TEST: Every byLocale entry passed one mechanical check before being written down: that locale never renders the same English value differently anywhere else in lang/. A counter-example means a translator DID translate it, so it is real work and stays counted. That is why `Status` is allowlisted for nl (30 of 30 occurrences identical) but not for de/pl/pt, which also produce Stand / Stan / Estado; and why Irish has no entries at all — it borrows far less than the continental languages, so all ~30 of its remaining values are genuinely untranslated. Passing the check is necessary, not sufficient: a value that is only ever left untranslated also has no counter-example, so each entry is additionally a per-value judgement that a translator would leave it alone. Placeholder-only values (`:community`, `:xp XP`, `:value%`) are global because there is nothing in them to translate; so are language endonyms, which are by definition written the same in every language.
